prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: C#Cc1cccc(Nc2ncnc3cc(OCCOC)c(OCCOC)cc23)c1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL203

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of histidine-tagged human recombinant cytoplasmic domain of EGFR expressed in baculovirus infected insect Sf9 cells after 1 hr by DELFIA/time-resolved fluorometric analysis
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: Sf9
  Test type: In vitro

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of autophosphorylation of His6-tagged EGFR cytoplasmic domain (unknown origin) expressed in Sf9 cells by DELFIA time resolved fluorometry
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: Sf9

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.85, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for inhibition of EGFR cytoplasmic domain autophosphorylation using the same expression system (His-tagged, Sf9 cells), same detection method (DELFIA time-resolved fluorometry), same assay type (biochemical, in vitro), and same confidence score, making them highly comparable."}
